title: SB 202 (2021) Election Integrity Act of 2021 (2021-2022) — omnibus election law including ID number or ID copy on absentee requests
operative_text:
Absentee ID (secondary: Wikipedia): Requires absentee voters to supply a driver's license or state ID number, the last four digits of their Social Security number, or a photocopy of an accepted ID when requesting a ballot.
Signature match replaced: Replaces signature-match verification of absentee ballots by poll workers.
Drop boxes: Codifies permanent drop boxes for general elections and requires at least one per county.
Absentee request window: Moves the request deadline from four days to eleven days before Election Day.
Unsolicited absentee applications: Bars state and local officials from sending unsolicited absentee ballot request forms to registered voters.
Early voting: Mandates three weeks of in-person early voting, including two Saturdays and optionally two Sundays.
State control of county boards and State Election Board composition: Lets the State Board of Elections replace a county board with a state-chosen administrator if the State Board deems the county board to be performing poorly.
Runoffs and special elections: Shortens the Senate runoff period from nine weeks to four weeks.
Long lines: Requires counties with precincts of more than 2,000 voters that had waits over an hour in 2020 to add a voting station or add staff or equipment.
Food and water: Makes it illegal to give free food or water to voters waiting in line within 150 feet of polling locations or 25 feet of voting lines
Wrong-precinct provisional ballots: Eliminates the option of casting a provisional ballot at the wrong polling location, requiring voters to go to the correct precinct.
Third-party funding: Prohibits outside, third-party funding of elections.
Other (litigation coverage): A general ban on photographing voted ballots (preliminarily enjoined in August 2021).
